John W. Campbell, Invaders from the Infinite.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/john-w-campbell/invaders-from-the-infinite

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- John W. Campbell, the author and annotator, died 1971 (Wikidata Q435056, P570 = 1971-07-11).

First publication of the text used: 1932 (SE colophon: 'Invaders from the Infinite was published in 1932 by John W. Campbell').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1932 (SE colophon), which is after 1930, so this bullet relies on Standard Ebooks' statement of rights quoted below.
- Country of origin (United States): the text first appeared in the United States. The Wikipedia article for the novel (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invaders_from_the_Infinite) says it expands stories first published in the American magazine Amazing Stories Quarterly, and that the book was published in 1961 by Gnome Press and Fantasy Press. The origin is the United States, the same country as the bullet above, so no other country's term applies.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

- SE colophon: Invaders from the Infinite was published in 1932 by John W. Campbell.
- Wikidata Q435056 (John W. Campbell), P570 = 1971-07-11; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Campbell
